questions.question: The speed of a train is 108 km/h. The distance covered by the train in 11 seconds will be:
questions.solution:
**GIVEN :**

Speed = 108 km/h

Time = 11 seconds

**FORMULA USED:**

Distance = Speed × Time 

**CALCULATION :**

Speed = 108 km/h 

To convert km/h into m/s multiply the number by 5/18.

 speed = 108 × 5/18 m/s = 30 m/s.

Distance = Speed × Time = 30 × 11 = 330 m

**Hence, the distance covered by the train is 330m.**

questions.question: P and Q start running in opposite directions on a circular track from the same point. If their speeds are 10 m/s and 8 m/s, respectively, then after what time will they meet if the length of the track is 1620 m?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two persons run in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 10 + 8 = 18 m/s

Time taken to meet = Total track distance ÷ Relative speed

Time = 1620 ÷ 18 = 90 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 90 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/116b1ffd88d8f5fff8b40f9cda091b65c1c6db1f92fed6f40d7aa0f770237b50.png] 

**Given:**

Speed of P = 10 m/s

Speed of Q = 8 m/s

Length of the track (Total Distance) = 1620 m

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 + 8

⇒ Relative Speed = 18 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = 1620 ÷ 18

⇒ Time taken to meet = 90 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 90 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (v₁ + v₂).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the absolute difference of their individual speeds (|v₁ − v₂|).

Time to Meet at the Starting Point

The time taken for two persons to meet exactly at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by them to complete one full round.

Distinct Meeting Points

If two persons run at speeds 'a' and 'b' (where a and b are co-prime integers), they meet at (a + b) distinct points if moving in opposite directions, and |a − b| distinct points if moving in the same direction.
</p

questions.question: In a circular race of 1500 m. Anil and Bilal start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. When will they meet again for the first time on the track when they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

The distance of the circular path race = 1500 m

Anil's speed = 36 km/hr

Bilal's speed = 54 km/hr

Both start from the same point and at the same time and run in the same direction.

**Concept used:**

When A and B are moving with x km/hr and y km/hr, respectively

In the same direction,

then Relative speed = (x - y) km/hr

In the opposite direction,

then Relative speed = (x + y) km/hr

**Formula used:**

Conversion of km/hr to m/sec

1 km/hr = (5/18) m/sec

Distance = speed x time

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

They are moving in the same direction,

Relative speed = (54 - 36) km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 18 km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 18 x (5/18) m/sec

⇒ Relative speed = 5 m/sec

As we know that,

Distance = Speed x time

⇒ Time = Distance/speed

⇒ Time = 1500/5 = 300 sec

**∴ The answer is 300 sec.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Formula used:

Time taken to meet for the 1st time = Length of the track/Relative Speed

Time taken = L/u+v, when moving in the opposite direction.

Time taken = L/u-v, when moving in the same direction.

Where, L = Length of the track

u = Speed of A, v = speed of B

1 km/hr = (5/18) m/sec

Calculation:

Time taken to meet for the 1st time = 1500/[(54-36) x (5/18)]

So, time taken for meeting for the 1st time = 1500/5 = 300 sec

∴ The answer is 300 sec.

questions.question: In a circular race of 4800m, A and B start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h. When will they meet again for the first time on the track if they are running in the opposite direction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in opposite direction = 36 + 54 = 90 km/h = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s.

Time to meet for the first time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 4800 ÷ 25 = 192 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 192 second.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the circular track = 4800 m

Speed of A = 36 km/h

Speed of B = 54 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/faa7231fc091da6e0b365ac3691a75486a52bee979089951a61b34bcded79ded.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = Speed of A + Speed of B

Time taken to meet = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of A in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

⇒ Speed of B in m/s = 54 × (5/18) = 15 m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 + 15 = 25 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 4800 ÷ 25

⇒ Time = 192 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 192 second.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting for the first time anywhere on the track

Time = Length of track ÷ Relative Speed. The relative speed is the sum of their speeds if moving in opposite directions, and difference of their speeds if moving in the same direction.

Meeting for the first time at the starting point

Time = LCM of individual times taken to complete one full round (LCM of T₁, T₂, ...). This applies irrespective of the direction of motion.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s directly, multiply the given speed by 5/18. Conversely, to convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: The ratio between the speeds of two cars is 5 ∶ 7. If the first car runs 200 km in 4 hours, then what is the speed of second car?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Speed ratio of two cars: 5 ∶ 7

Distance covered by the first car: 200 km

Time taken by the first car: 4 hours

**Concept:**

Ratio of speeds and calculation of speed.

**Calculation:**

⇒ The speed of the first car = 200 km / 4 hours = 50 km/h.

⇒ If speed ratio is 5 ∶ 7, then the speed of second car is 7/5 × speed of first car.

⇒ Speed of second car = 7/5 × 50 km/h = 70 km/h.

**Therefore, the speed of the second car is 70 km/h.**

questions.question: A man travelled by car from city A to city B at a speed of 24 km/h and returned from city B to city A at 16 km/h. Find his average speed over the whole journey.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A man travelled by car from city A to city B at a speed of 24 km/h and returned from city B to city A at 16 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Time taken = Distance/Speed

Average speed = Total distance travel/Total time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the cities A and B be 'd'.

Then, time taken for the car to move from city A to city B at a speed of 24 km/h is (d)/(24) hours.

And, time taken for the car to move from city B to city A at a speed of 16 km/h is (d)/(16) hours.

Average speed = (2d)/(frac{d){24}+(d)/(16)} = (2× 24×16)/(40)=19.2 km/h.

**∴ The average speed of the man for the whole journey is 19.2 km/h**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Calculation:**

Average speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂)/ S₁ + S₂

⇒ (2 × 24 × 16)/ 40

⇒ (16 × 12)/ 10 = 19.2 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 km/h.**

questions.question: A policeman is chasing a thief at a speed of 82 km/h. The thief is 1300 m away and is running at a speed of 64 km/h. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief if both are riding on bikes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since both the policeman and the thief are moving in the same direction, relative speed = 82 − 64 = 18 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s.

Time required to cover 1300 m gap = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 1300 ÷ 5 = 260 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 260 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/459e8a3558179988894b40dc8d137de344ddb061ab6ac577bf8c6f0cd38428ab.png] 

**Given:**

Speed of Policeman (S₁) = 82 km/h

Speed of Thief (S₂) = 64 km/h

Initial distance between them (D) = 1300 m

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in the same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 82 − 64 = 18 km/h

⇒ Convert speed into m/s: 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 1300 ÷ 5 = 260 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 260 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average speed is the Total Distance Covered divided by Total Time Taken. If a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).
</p

questions.question: A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours. Find the distance between the two stations
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours.

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the station X and Y be d and the initial speed of the train be v

Then, d = 6v

When the speed of the train is reduced by 13km/h, the equation can be written as d = 9(v-13).

Substituting v=(d)/(6) in the above equation and solving for d,

d=9( (d)/(6) -13)

d=(3d)/(2) -117

d = 234km

**∴ The distance between the two stations is 234 km.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Let the initial speed be x

Distance = Speed × Time 

According to the question,

⇒ x × 6 = (x - 13) × 9

⇒ 6x = 9x - 117

⇒ 3x = 117

⇒ x = 39 kmph

Distance = 39 × 6 = 234 km. 

∴ The distance between the two stations is 234 km.

questions.question: A bus driver must complete a 240 km trip in 4 hours. If he averages 70 km an hour for the first 3 hours of his trip. how fast must he travel (in km/h) in the last/final hour?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A bus driver must complete a 240 km trip in 4 hours. He averages 70 km/h for the first 3 hours of his trip.

**Concept:**

To find the required speed for the last hour, we need to determine the remaining distance and then calculate the speed needed to cover that distance in the remaining time.

**Calculation:**

Total distance to be covered = 240 km

Total time available = 4 hours

Distance covered in the first 3 hours:

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 70 km/h × 3 hours

⇒ Distance = 210 km

Remaining distance to be covered in the final hour:

⇒ Remaining distance = Total distance - Distance covered in the first 3 hours

⇒ Remaining distance = 240 km - 210 km

⇒ Remaining distance = 30 km

Speed required to cover the remaining distance in the final hour:

⇒ Speed = Distance / Time

⇒ Speed = 30 km / 1 hour

⇒ Speed = 30 km/h

**∴ The bus driver must travel at 30 km/h in the last hour.**

questions.question: Two athletes are participating in a race on a circular track of 220 m. Ravi runs at the speed of 22 m/s, while Kapil runs at the speed of 11 m/s. They start from the same point, at the same time and in the same direction. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When running in the same direction on a circular track, the relative speed is the difference of their speeds.

Relative Speed = 22 − 11 = 11 m/s

Time to meet = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 220 ÷ 11 = 20 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 20 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b07ca61b1611a24a1b24e89d5858bc5ea0845772d8697d19a12923289e99abc8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative speed (same direction) = Speed 1 − Speed 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 22 − 11 = 11 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time taken = 220 ÷ 11

⇒ Time taken = 20 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 20 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The time taken to meet exactly at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the individual times taken by each runner to complete one full round.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies move in opposite directions around a track, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

When running in the same direction, the total number of distinct meeting points on the circular track is the difference of their speeds when expressed in their simplest ratio.

questions.question: A thief pursued by a policeman was 150 m ahead at the start. If the ratio of the speed of the policeman to that of the thief was 5 : 4, then how far (distance in metres) could the thief go before he is caught by the policeman?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the time traveled is constant, the ratio of distances covered is directly equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of distances (Policeman : Thief) = Ratio of speeds = 5 : 4

Difference in distance ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 unit

This 1 unit difference corresponds to the initial gap of 150 m.

Distance covered by the thief = 4 units = 4 × 150 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between the policeman and the thief = 150 m

Ratio of speeds (Policeman : Thief) = 5 : 4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f7c426194eb344902d1d5298451d3b3e2043f5b259ee938cc1b85a3bc9c3f17.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of the policeman be 5x m/s and the thief be 4x m/s.

⇒ Relative speed = 5x − 4x = x m/s

⇒ Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = Initial Distance Gap ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Catching Time = 150 ÷ x seconds

⇒ Distance covered by the thief before getting caught = Speed of thief × Catching Time

⇒ Distance = 4x × (150 ÷ x)

⇒ Distance = 4 × 150 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂ (where S₁ > S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects travel towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Constant Time Property

If two moving bodies travel for exactly the same amount of time, the distance covered by each is directly proportional to their respective speeds (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂).
</p

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 195 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 22 km/h and that of the policeman is 27 km/h, then how far would the thief have run (in m) before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the time taken by both to meet is the same, the ratio of distances covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of speeds = Policeman : Thief = 27 : 22

Difference in ratio = 27 − 22 = 5 units

This 5 units represents the initial gap of 195 m ⇒ 1 unit = 195 ÷ 5 = 39 m

Distance covered by the thief = 22 units = 22 × 39 = 858 m

**∴ The correct answer is 858 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6eda407eba74eefafb11bfeaa1978b9c274c112acc0da11c671fef9e03aef76.png] 

**Given:**

Initial distance between Policeman and Thief = 195 m

Speed of Policeman (SP) = 27 km/h

Speed of Thief (ST) = 22 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 27 − 22 = 5 km/h

⇒ Convert Relative Speed into m/s = 5 × (5 ÷ 18) = 25 ÷ 18 m/s

⇒ Time taken by Policeman to overtake = 195 ÷ (25 ÷ 18)

⇒ Time = (195 × 18) ÷ 25 = 140.4 seconds

⇒ Speed of Thief in m/s = 22 × (5 ÷ 18) = 55 ÷ 9 m/s

⇒ Distance covered by the Thief = Speed × Time = (55 ÷ 9) × 140.4

⇒ Distance = 55 × 15.6 = 858 m

**∴ The correct answer is 858 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions, relative speed is their sum (S₁ + S₂).

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by (5 ÷ 18). Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).

Proportionality of Distance and Speed

If the time taken is constant, the distance traveled by an object is directly proportional to its speed (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂). This allows solving chase problems instantly using ratio methods.
</p

questions.question: Two cities A and B are 135 km apart on a straight track. One car starts from A at 8 a.m. and travels towards B at 25 km/h. Another car starts from B at 9 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 30 km/h. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
__***The correct answer is (11a.m.)***__

__****Key Points__** -*

Suppose they meet ***after x hours*** after 8 a.m.

Distance covered by ***A after x hours*** = 25x km.

Distance covered by ***B after (x-1) hours* **=30(x-1) km.

 ***Distance = Time * speed***

 135 = 25x + 30(x-1)

 135 = 25x + 30x - 30

 135 = 55x - 30

 135 + 30 = 55x 

 165/55 = x

 __*** i.e , x = 3 hours ***__

 ***The two cars will meet after 3 hours ; 8a.m. + 3hours = 11 a.m. ***

** __HENCE ,THE CORRECT ANSWER IS 11 A.M.__***

questions.question: A vehicle is going at one-fourth of its usual speed and it takes an extra 45 minutes to reach its destination. Its usual time to cover the same distance is:

New speed = 1/4 of usual speed

Extra time = 45 minutes = 0.75 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Since new speed is 1/4 of the usual, it takes 4 times longer to cover the same distance.

Let usual time = T hours

New time = 4T

Extra time taken = New time - usual time

⇒ 0.75 = 4T - T

⇒ 3T = 0.75

⇒ T = 0.75/3

⇒ T = 0.25 hours

**Usual time to cover the distance = 0.25 hours or 15 minutes**

questions.question: A thief stole jewellery from a shop at 8:15 p.m. and left on a bike at a speed of 60 km/h. The police were informed at 8:30 p.m. If the police want to arrest the thief at 9:00 p.m., what should be the minimum speed of the police jeep?

Time when the thief stole the jewellery = 8:15 p.m.

Speed of thief's bike = 60 km/h

Time when police were informed = 8:30 p.m.

**Formula used:**

Minimum speed of police officer = {Distance between the thief and the police} over {Time taken by police to reach the thief}

**Calculation:**

If the thief left at 8:15 p.m. and the police wants to catch him at 9:00 p.m., the time for which the thief was on the bike = 45 minutes = 3 over 4 hours = 0.75 hours

Distance travelled by the thief = 60 km/h × 0.75 h = 45 km 

Time taken by the police to reach the thief = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

Thus, minimum speed of the police jeep should be = 45\: {km} over 0.5 \:{h} = (45 × 2) km/h = 90 km/h 

**∴ The minimum speed of the police jeep should be 90 km/h.**

questions.question: In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. After how much time will they meet next?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since A and B are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds.

Relative Speed = 12 − 6 = 6 m/s

Time to meet next = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 840 ÷ 6 = 140 s

**∴ The correct answer is 140 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Length of circular track (D) = 840 m

⇒ Speed of A (SA) = 6 m/s

⇒ Speed of B (SB) = 12 m/s

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Relative Speed (same direction) = |SB − SA|

⇒ Time to meet = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfa0795d833bb6d34bedbbfdc5b2c502cf3c5028b456e2ed1d9ff605c01e8df1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 m/s − 6 m/s = 6 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = 840 ÷ 6

⇒ Time to meet = 140 s

**∴ The correct answer is 140 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

First Meeting Anywhere on Track

When two persons run in the same direction, they meet for the first time when the faster person covers exactly one more round than the slower person. Time = Length of Track ÷ Relative Speed.

First Meeting at Starting Point

The time taken to meet for the first time at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by each person to complete one full round. Time = LCM(T₁, T₂).

Running in Opposite Directions

If two runners move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). The time for their first meeting anywhere on the track is Track Length ÷ (S₁ + S₂).
</p
